title: cell-curator neutral prediction table
description: Describes the header of a neutral prediction table: a per-cell export any annotation system can produce, which `cell-curator benchmark evaluate` scores without knowing which system wrote it. `optional_columns` is permissive because unknown columns are ignored, so a vendor may add its own. `scored_optional_columns` enumerates the columns the evaluator actually reads and `scored_optional_column_metrics` says what each one is for; a column present but absent from those two changes no published metric. That distinction is the reason the enumeration exists: the contract used to list no optional column at all, so an exporter following it could not know that `confidence` was what made the risk-coverage curve computable, nor that CL identifiers turn on a metric that cannot be produced without a local ontology snapshot.

optional_columns.description: Every optional column present in the table, scored or not.

allOf.description: `true_path` and `predicted_path` are read only as a pair.
`true_mixed` and `predicted_mixed` are read only as a pair.
`true_split_decision` and `predicted_split_decision` are read only as a pair.

Either CL spelling enables `ontology_distance_error`, `descendant_accuracy` and `relaxed_accuracy`, and either spelling then requires `cell-curator benchmark evaluate --ontology` with a local Cell Ontology snapshot: the evaluator refuses to report the metrics for a table it cannot measure rather than substituting another one. The same pair is what `cell_curator.sweep_benchmark_risk_coverage` scores a curve against, under `agreement="descendant"` (a prediction counts when it is the truth or a more specific subtype) or `agreement="relaxed"` (also credits a coarser answer).

scored_optional_columns.description: The optional columns the evaluator reads at runtime.

confidence.description: Finite and within [0, 1] or the table is refused. This is also the axis of the risk-coverage sweep.

scored_optional_column_metrics.description: Each column and the `BenchmarkResult` fields it can move. `accuracy`, `macro_f1`, `micro_f1`, `per_type` (precision, recall, F1, and support for every label), `coverage`, `selective_accuracy`, `coverage_risk`, and the `Unknown` precision, recall, and F1 come from the three required columns alone: `relaxed_accuracy` is reported beside `accuracy` rather than in place of it, so the exact-label number is still there to disagree with.

carried_unscored_columns.description: Columns the shipped fixture carries for a human reader. They are permitted and change no metric, which is why they are named here rather than left in a header to look like measurements.
